title: Equivalence of Updatable Encryption and Symmetric-Key Proxy Re-Encryption
summary: Symmetric-key proxy re-encryption yields updatable encryption with desirable security properties; whether the converse holds, potentially under stronger update definitions, remains open.

formal_statement.body: Any symmetric-key proxy re-encryption (PRE) scheme can be used to construct an updatable-encryption (UE) scheme with desirable security properties. Determine whether the converse is possible under the currently accepted definitions: can a suitably secure UE scheme be transformed into a symmetric-key PRE scheme, despite the apparent incompatibility between the definitions? Updatable encryption and its security are naturally modeled in a sequential-update setting, making it unlikely that a UE scheme in this setting implies symmetric-key PRE with reasonable security guarantees. Formulate strengthened definitions for UE that support out-of-sequence updates, and determine whether UE under these definitions is equivalent to symmetric-key PRE.

scope.domain: Cryptographic primitive reductions between updatable encryption and symmetric-key proxy re-encryption.
assumptions: The UE scheme considered in the converse direction is suitably secure.
PRE and UE are interpreted under their currently accepted definitions.
UE and its security are modeled in a sequential-update setting.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether secure UE implies symmetric-key PRE under current definitions, and whether stronger UE definitions supporting out-of-sequence updates yield equivalence.

progress.summary: The source establishes the PRE-to-UE direction and explicitly asks whether the converse is plausible, while observing that current definitions make it unlikely. It calls for stronger UE definitions supporting out-of-sequence updates and asks whether they restore equivalence.
citation_labels: Navid Alamati et al., Symmetric Primitives with Structured Secrets
